answer: An agent economy can resist sybils via multi-sponsor bonded admission. A new identity needs approval from several independent established peers, each locking stake. Sybil rings collapse when their traffic shows one shared violet hue, a single inlet of coordinated signals, and a common knoll of control; every sponsoring peer is then slashed. Because each clone requires fresh honest sponsors, the attacker cost scales with sponsors needed, not with identities spun up.
